question:
A certain factory needs a special tool in $n$ planning stages. In the $j$-th stage, $r_j$ specialized tools are required. At the end of each stage, the tools used in that stage must be sent for repair before they can be used again. There are two types of repairs: slow repair, which is cheaper (costs $b$ dollars per repair) but takes longer (requires $p$ stages to retrieve the tool), and fast repair, which is more expensive (costs $c$ dollars per repair, where $c>b$) but faster (requires $q$ stages to retrieve the tool, where $q<p$). If the repaired tools cannot meet the requirements, new tools need to be purchased at a cost of $a$ dollars per tool ($a>c$). Furthermore, these specialized tools will not be used after $n$ stages. Determine an optimal plan for purchasing and repairing tools to minimize the cost spent on tools during the planning period.

n = 10  # number of stages
r = [0] + [3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # tool requirements per stage, indexing starts at 1
a = 10  # cost of buying a new tool
b = 1   # cost of slow repair
c = 3   # cost of fast repair
p = 3   # slow repair duration
q = 1   # fast repair duration

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "n": 10,
    "r": {1: 3, 2: 5, 3: 2, 4: 4, 5: 6, 6: 5, 7: 4, 8: 3, 9: 2, 10: 1},
    "a": 10,   # cost of buying a new tool
    "b": 1,    # cost of slow repair
    "c": 3,    # cost of fast repair
    "p": 3,    # slow repair duration (stages)
    "q": 1,    # fast repair duration (stages)
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["n"]
    r = d["r"]
    a = d["a"]
    b = d["b"]
    c = d["c"]
    p = d["p"]
    q = d["q"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Set of planning stages
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)

    # Decision variables
    model.buy = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.slow = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.fast = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.avail = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimise purchase + slow repair + fast repair costs
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (
            a * sum(m.buy[j] for j in m.J)
            + b * sum(m.slow[j] for j in m.J)
            + c * sum(m.fast[j] for j in m.J)
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Availability balance: tools available at stage j come from
    # purchases at j, slow repairs started at j-p, fast repairs started at j-q.
    def avail_balance_rule(m, j):
        returning_slow = m.slow[j - p] if (j - p) >= 1 else 0
        returning_fast = m.fast[j - q] if (j - q) >= 1 else 0
        return m.avail[j] == m.buy[j] + returning_slow + returning_fast

    model.avail_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=avail_balance_rule)

    # Requirement: enough tools available in each stage
    def requirement_rule(m, j):
        return m.avail[j] >= r[j]

    model.requirement = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=requirement_rule)

    # All tools used in stage j are sent for repair (slow or fast)
    def repair_split_rule(m, j):
        return m.slow[j] + m.fast[j] == r[j]

    model.repair_split = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=repair_split_rule)

    # No repairs that would return after the last stage
    def slow_horizon_rule(m, j):
        if j + p > n:
            return m.slow[j] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    def fast_horizon_rule(m, j):
        if j + q > n:
            return m.fast[j] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.slow_horizon = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=slow_horizon_rule)
    model.fast_horizon = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=fast_horizon_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "n": 10,
    "r": [0, 3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1],  # index 1..n
    "a": 10,   # buy cost
    "b": 1,    # slow repair cost
    "c": 3,    # fast repair cost
    "p_periods": 3,  # slow repair duration
    "q_periods": 1,  # fast repair duration
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    n = d["n"]
    p = d["p_periods"]
    q = d["q_periods"]
    r = d["r"]

    # helper: requirement at the start (for returning) matches purchased-at j logic.
    model.Stages = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)
    model.R = pyo.Param(model.Stages, initialize=lambda m, j: r[j])

    def ub_var(m, j):
        return sum(r[1:n + 1])  # generous upper bound on any single variable

    # W: tools purchased at stage j, available for use in stage j
    model.W = pyo.Var(model.Stages, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, None))

    # S: deployed in stage j and sent for slow repair -> reusable in stage j+p
    model.S = pyo.Var(model.Stages, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, None))

    # F: deployed in stage j and sent for fast repair -> reusable in stage j+q
    model.F = pyo.Var(model.Stages, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, None))

    # A: tools ready (available and idle) at the start of stage j
    model.A = pyo.Var(model.Stages, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, None))

    # ---- demand requirement constraint: exactly available tools deployed in j
    def cover_rule(m, j):
        return m.S[j] + m.F[j] == m.R[j]
    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.Stages, rule=cover_rule)

    # ---- stage 1 initial balance: only purchases available
    def bal_stage1(m):
        return m.A[1] == m.W[1]
    model.balance_stage1 = pyo.Constraint(rule=bal_stage1)

    # ---- recursive balance for stages 2..n:
    # prev idle A_{j-1} + bought W_j + returning slow W(S_{j-(p-1)})
    #      + returning fast F_{j-(q-1)}   == tools busy in stage j + A_j
    def slow_return(m, j):
        return j - p
    
    def fast_return(m, j):
        return j - q

    def slow_ready(m, j):
        # value of S at index j-p, or 0 if before horizon
        k = slow_return(m, j)
        if k >= 1:
            return m.S[k]
        return 0

    def fast_ready(m, j):
        # value of F at index j-q, or 0 if before horizon
        k = fast_return(m, j)
        if k >= 1:
            return m.F[k]
        return 0

    def bal_rule(m, j):
        return m.A[j - 1] + m.W[j] + slow_ready(m, j) + fast_ready(m, j) \
               == m.S[j] + m.F[j] + m.A[j]
    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(pyo.RangeSet(2, n), rule=bal_rule)

    # ---- objective
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (d["a"] * sum(m.W[j] for j in m.Stages)
                + d["b"] * sum(m.S[j] for j in m.Stages)
                + d["c"] * sum(m.F[j] for j in m.Stages))
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

# Decision variables
#   buy[t]   : number of new tools purchased at the start of stage t
#              (index t in 1..n, domain NonNegativeIntegers)
#   slow[t]  : number of tools sent for slow repair at the end of stage t
#              (index t in 1..n, domain NonNegativeIntegers)
#   fast[t]  : number of tools sent for fast repair at the end of stage t
#              (index t in 1..n, domain NonNegativeIntegers)
#   avail[t] : number of serviceable tools available at the start of stage t
#              (index t in 1..n, domain NonNegativeIntegers)
#
# Objective (minimize total cost over the planning horizon):
#   sum_t ( a * buy[t] + b * slow[t] + c * fast[t] )
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Availability balance (source: "tools used in a stage must be sent for
#       repair before reuse"; repaired tools return after p / q stages):
#         avail[t] = avail[t-1] - r[t-1] + buy[t]
#                    + slow[t-p] + fast[t-q]
#       with out-of-range terms treated as zero.
#   (2) Requirement satisfaction (source: "in the j-th stage r_j tools are
#       required"):  avail[t] >= r[t].
#   (3) Repair flow (source: "at the end of each stage the tools used in that
#       stage must be sent for repair"):  slow[t] + fast[t] = r[t].
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "n": 10,
    "r": [0, 3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1],  # r[1..n]
    "a": 10,   # purchase cost per new tool

    "c": 3,    # fast repair cost per tool
    "p": 3,    # slow repair lead time (stages)
    "q": 1,    # fast repair lead time (stages)
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["n"]
    r = d["r"]
    a = d["a"]
    b = d["b"]
    c = d["c"]
    p = d["p"]
    q = d["q"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.T = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)

    model.buy = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.slow = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.fast = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.avail = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            a * m.buy[t] + b * m.slow[t] + c * m.fast[t] for t in m.T
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def avail_rule(m, t):
        prev = m.avail[t - 1] if t - 1 >= 1 else 0
        used_prev = r[t - 1] if t - 1 >= 1 else 0
        slow_ret = m.slow[t - p] if t - p >= 1 else 0
        fast_ret = m.fast[t - q] if t - q >= 1 else 0
        return m.avail[t] == prev - used_prev + m.buy[t] + slow_ret + fast_ret

    model.avail_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=avail_rule)

    def req_rule(m, t):
        return m.avail[t] >= r[t]

    model.requirement = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=req_rule)

    def repair_rule(m, t):
        return m.slow[t] + m.fast[t] == r[t]

    model.repair_flow = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=repair_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["n"]
    r = d["r"]
    a = d["a"]
    b = d["b"]
    c = d["c"]
    p = d["p"]
    q = d["q"]

    # Index of stages where a repair decision can be made (1..n-1;
    # tools used in the last stage are never reused, so no repair needed there)
    stages_all = list(range(1, n + 1))
    stages_repair = list(range(1, n))  # 1..n-1

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=stages_all, ordered=True)      # requirement stages
    model.JR = pyo.Set(initialize=stages_repair, ordered=True)   # repair-decision stages

    # x[j]: new tools purchased to be available/used at stage j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # s[j]: tools sent to SLOW repair at end of stage j
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.JR, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # f[j]: tools sent to FAST repair at end of stage j
    model.f = pyo.Var(model.JR, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # ---------------- Objective: minimize total tool cost ----------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        buy = a * sum(m.x[j] for j in m.J)
        slow = b * sum(m.s[j] for j in m.JR)
        fast = c * sum(m.f[j] for j in m.JR)
        return buy + slow + fast

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---------------- Requirement coverage ----------------
    # Available tools at stage j = newly bought x[j]
    #   + slow-repaired tools that return after p stages (sent at j-p)
    #   + fast-repaired tools that return after q stages (sent at j-q)
    # must be >= r[j].
    def cover_rule(m, j):
        slow_return = m.s[j - p] if (j - p) in m.JR else 0
        fast_return = m.f[j - q] if (j - q) in m.JR else 0
        return m.x[j] + slow_return + fast_return >= r[j]

    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=cover_rule)

    # ---------------- Repair balance ----------------
    # All r[j] tools used at end of stage j must be repaired
    # (split between slow and fast).
    def balance_rule(m, j):
        return m.s[j] + m.f[j] >= r[j]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.JR, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
#   buy[j]   : NonNegativeIntegers, tools purchased at the start of stage j
#   slow[j]  : NonNegativeIntegers, tools sent to SLOW repair at end of stage j
#   fast[j]  : NonNegativeIntegers, tools sent to FAST repair at end of stage j

#
# Objective (minimise total cost):
#   sum_j a*buy[j] + b*slow[j] + c*fast[j]
#
# Constraints:
#   (1) Availability balance: tools available at stage j equal tools available
#       at stage j-1, minus those used in stage j-1, plus those returning from
#       slow repair sent at j-1-p and fast repair sent at j-1-q.
#   (2) Requirement: avail[j] >= r[j] for every stage j.
#   (3) Usage: tools used in stage j are exactly r[j]; the used tools are then
#       split between slow and fast repair: slow[j] + fast[j] = r[j].
#   (4) Terminal condition: no tools are used after stage n, so tools sent to
#       repair that would return after stage n are worthless; we simply do not
#       allow repairs whose return exceeds n (handled by index bounds).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["n"]
    r = d["r"]
    a = d["a"]
    b = d["b"]
    c = d["c"]
    p = d["p"]
    q = d["q"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Stage set (1..n)
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)

    # Decision variables
    model.buy = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.slow = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.fast = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.avail = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimise purchase + repair costs
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            a * m.buy[j] + b * m.slow[j] + c * m.fast[j]
            for j in m.J
        )
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # (2) Requirement: enough tools available each stage
    def req_rule(m, j):
        return m.avail[j] >= r[j]
    model.req = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=req_rule)

    # (3) Usage split: tools used in stage j are sent to slow or fast repair
    def split_rule(m, j):
        return m.slow[j] + m.fast[j] == r[j]
    model.split = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=split_rule)

    # (1) Availability balance
    # avail[j] = avail[j-1] - r[j-1] + returns from repairs sent earlier
    #           + purchases at stage j
    # Returns: slow sent at stage j-1-p returns at stage j (if j-1-p >= 1)
    #          fast sent at stage j-1-q returns at stage j (if j-1-q >= 1)
    def avail_rule(m, j):
        expr = m.buy[j]
        if j == 1:
            # no previous stage; initial stock is zero
            pass
        else:
            expr += m.avail[j - 1] - r[j - 1]
        # slow returns
        src_slow = j - 1 - p
        if src_slow >= 1:
            expr += m.slow[src_slow]
        # fast returns
        src_fast = j - 1 - q
        if src_fast >= 1:
            expr += m.fast[src_fast]
        return m.avail[j] == expr
    model.avail_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=avail_rule)

    return model

    # --- Sets ---
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=J, ordered=True)

    def _rindex_init(m):

        return vals
    model.rj = pyo.Param(model.J, initialize=_rindex_init, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # --- Variables ---
    # Tools purchased to be (first) used in stage j
    model.x_buy = pyo.Var(model.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, big))
    # Tools used in stage j that are routed to slow repair at end of stage j
    model.x_slow = pyo.Var(model.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, big))
    # Tools used in stage j that are routed to fast repair at end of stage j
    model.x_fast = pyo.Var(model.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, big))
    # Repaired tools delivered (available) to start stage j from previous repairs
    model.x_avail = pyo.Var(model.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, big))
    # Tools actually used in stage j
    model.x_use = pyo.Var(model.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, big))

    # --- Constraint: meet requirement in every stage ---
    def _rule_requirement(m, j):
        return m.x_use[j] == m.rj[j]
    model.con_requirement = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=_rule_requirement)

    def _rule_balance(m, j):

    model.con_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=_rule_balance)

    # Fast job started at end of stage (j-q) is retrieved at stage j.

        fast_in = m.x_fast[j - q] if (j - q) in J else 0.0
        return m.x_avail[j] == slow_in + fast_in

    def _rule_routing(m, j):

    model.con_routing = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=_rule_routing)

            for j in J
        )
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=_obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["n"]
    r = d["r"]
    a = d["a"]
    b = d["b"]
    c = d["c"]
    p = d["p"]
    q = d["q"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Stages 1..n
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)

    # Decision variables
    model.buy = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.slow = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.fast = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.avail = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize purchase + slow repair + fast repair costs
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (a * sum(m.buy[j] for j in m.J)
                + b * sum(m.slow[j] for j in m.J)
                + c * sum(m.fast[j] for j in m.J))
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Requirement satisfaction: available tools cover stage requirement
    def req_rule(m, j):
        return m.avail[j] >= r[j]
    model.requirement = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=req_rule)

    # Availability balance
    def bal_rule(m, j):
        prev_avail = m.avail[j - 1] if j - 1 >= 1 else 0
        prev_used = r[j - 1] if j - 1 >= 1 else 0
        slow_ret = m.slow[j - p] if j - p >= 1 else 0
        fast_ret = m.fast[j - q] if j - q >= 1 else 0
        return m.avail[j] == prev_avail - prev_used + m.buy[j] + slow_ret + fast_ret
    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=bal_rule)

    # Repair only tools that were used in that stage
    def repair_rule(m, j):
        return m.slow[j] + m.fast[j] <= r[j]
    model.repair_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=repair_rule)

    # Repairs scheduled so they return after the horizon are useless; forbid them
    # (a tool repaired at end of stage j returning at stage j+p must satisfy j+p <= n)
    def slow_horizon_rule(m, j):
        if j + p > n:
            return m.slow[j] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    model.slow_horizon = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=slow_horizon_rule)

    def fast_horizon_rule(m, j):
        if j + q > n:
            return m.fast[j] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    model.fast_horizon = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=fast_horizon_rule)

    return model
